title: Usage & billing
description: Everything GOTCHA does uses credits. You see what's left, and how far it goes.

autoPurchase.unset: Nothing is set up for running low. GOTCHA will use the default: when the credit runs out, the AI stops answering.
autoPurchase.on: Buys more automatically when credit drops to {threshold}%.
autoPurchase.warnsFirst: You're told at {warn}% - before anything is bought, so there's time to decide.
autoPurchase.noCap: No monthly limit on automatic purchases.
autoPurchase.cap: Up to {cap} {currency} a month on automatic purchases. {spent} {currency} so far this cycle - {used}.

behavior.STOP_AI: When it runs out: the AI stops answering. People can still work.
behavior.HUMAN_ONLY: When it runs out: the AI stops and your team carries on as normal.
behavior.REQUIRE_APPROVAL: When it runs out: the AI keeps working, and every action waits for someone to approve it.
behavior.PREPAID_ONLY: Never buys more. GOTCHA runs on what you bought in advance and stops when it's gone.
behavior.PAYG: When it runs out: GOTCHA keeps working and the extra usage is billed at the end of the cycle.

autoPurchase.capIsNotACap: Note: with pay-as-you-go, the monthly limit stops automatic purchases - it doesn't stop the bill. Usage past zero is still charged at the end of the cycle.
autoPurchase.unsettable: Pay-as-you-go can't be switched on or off from here - it's set up by GOTCHA for you. The other options on this page can be changed.

option.payg: Pay as you go, up to a limit

autoPurchase.paygRate: Past your plan, extra use is billed at {rate} {currency} per credit at the end of the cycle.
autoPurchase.stopText: Nothing extra is charged. When credits run out, the rule under “If the limit is reached” takes over.
autoPurchase.alertLimit: When the monthly limit is hit
autoPurchase.subline: Which one is set, and what happens when credits run out.
autoPurchase.unsetShort: Nothing set yet - by default, the AI stops answering when credits run out.

pricing.title: Change plan
pricing.description: What you are on, what it costs, and what changing it would do.

pricing.converted: Shown in {display}. You are charged in {charged}.

pending.nothingChangesYet: Until then your plan, its features, its limits and its credits all stay exactly as they are.

change.deferred: A change to a cheaper plan takes effect at the end of your billing period, on {date}. Nothing changes before then.
change.irreversible: Once a change is scheduled, it cannot be called off here. Choosing a different plan replaces it, but there is no way back to no change at all - only a cancellation can be reversed from this screen, and a plan change cannot.
change.needsPermission: Changing the plan needs the Manage billing permission. Ask whoever administers your workspace.
change.noCard: There is no payment method on file, so an upgrade would be declined before anything changed. Add a card first - the upgrade will work straight afterwards.

packages.unavailable: We could not load credit packages just now.
packages.ineligible: Your plan does not include buying extra credit packages.
packages.none: There are no credit packages on sale right now.

expiry.PERIOD_END: These credits expire at the end of your billing period.

credits.unavailable: We could not load your credits just now.

awaitingGrant.lead: No credits have been issued for this billing period yet.
awaitingGrant.body: Your plan is contracted for {included} credits a period. The period that began on {date} has not had its credits granted, so the balance is zero - this is not credits you have spent.
awaitingGrant.short: Not granted yet for this period

consumption.withheld: We are not showing a usage figure for this period. The number the system reports counts expired credits as if they had been spent, so it would overstate what you actually used.

estimate.observedBasis: Measured from your own usage over the last {days} days.
estimate.planBasis: Based on your plan's published rate, not on your own usage.
estimate.partiallyAttributed: Only {pct}% of that usage was tied to a conversation - the rest was other AI work - so a per-conversation figure describes less of it than it looks.
estimate.awaitingGrant: Comes back once this period's credits are granted.
estimate.observedAverage: At your average of {avg} credits per conversation - your own usage, last {days} days

observed.noMetering: You have had {conversations} conversations in the last {days} days and no credits were recorded against them, so we cannot measure your own rate. That is about what has been metered, not about how much you have used GOTCHA.
observed.tooFewConversations: {conversations} conversations in the last {days} days is too few to measure a reliable rate from, so the estimate above uses your plan's published rate instead.

runout.label: Until renewal

buy.heading: Buy credits
